question: Why does QI dominate monotone RISE/FALL histories while QH dominates the final cumulative shape injection of WT_CYCLE: signed QI cancellation across monotone phases, a reversal-local QH mechanism, or a genuinely QH-dominant monotone phase?

model_policy.model: unchanged C0 enriched prescribed-H reduced geometry

phase_authority.source: BC2-A2 accepted H(t) strict interior zero-pressure crossing
phase_authority.partition_rule: maximal contiguous nonzero sign runs of dH = H_step - H_previous; no magnitude threshold

phases.physical_meaning: water-table depth H decreases; water table rises
water-table depth H increases; water table falls
water-table depth H decreases; water table rises

bias_ledger.primary_rank_metric: phase-local cumulative mass-neutral theta-shape injection RMS evaluated at that phase end geometry

accumulator_policy.phase_local: reset family storage-injection accumulator to zero at each phase start
accumulator_policy.cycle_running: also retain the unreset accumulator from cycle start and report it at steps 256, 512 and 768
accumulator_policy.reversal_singletons: report one-interval shape injection and signed flux bias for steps 257 and 513
accumulator_policy.tail_analysis: recompute phase-local ranks for FALL_TAIL and RISE_2_TAIL to distinguish a switch impulse from sustained phase bias

metrics: coherence abs(signed)/absolute per family and phase
phase-local cumulative shape RMS per family
cycle-running cumulative shape RMS at phase boundaries
family rank per phase and tail
QI directional cancellation ratio = 1 - abs(sum phase signed QI bias)/sum(abs(phase signed QI bias))
QH directional cancellation ratio defined identically
C3 hard additivity and physical-ledger residuals

H_CANCELLATION.statement: QI is rank-1 in each monotone phase and tail on both widths/routes, but its signed phase contributions change sign and cancel enough that whole-cycle QH becomes rank-1.
H_CANCELLATION.interpretation_if_supported: Whole-cycle QH dominance is primarily an aggregation/cancellation effect; it does not establish QH as the dominant local dynamic closure defect.

H_REVERSAL_LOCAL.statement: QI dominates non-reversal tails, but QH dominates one or both exact reversal intervals consistently across widths/routes.
H_REVERSAL_LOCAL.interpretation_if_supported: A distinct reversal-local qH mechanism exists in addition to monotone QI bias.

H_QH_PHASE.statement: QH is rank-1 in at least one sustained full phase or non-reversal tail on both numerical routes.
H_QH_PHASE.interpretation_if_supported: QH dominance cannot be explained only by cycle aggregation; a sustained regime-specific qH defect exists.

adjudication_policy.note: C4D maps mechanism only. It cannot authorize a closure correction.

progression: If H_CANCELLATION is supported without H_QH_PHASE, preregister teacher-forced QI oracle tests on monotone phases before designing any deployable closure.
If H_REVERSAL_LOCAL is supported, isolate the reversal interval physics in a separate counterfactual; do not add memory state unless response ambiguity requires it.
If H_QH_PHASE is supported, diagnose the common terminal shape/gradient reconstruction shared by qi and qH before treating the channels as independent parameters.
If width or numerical-route dependence dominates, stop closure intervention and refine numerical/reference qualification.
